title: Why the Bolsheviks survived, 1917–1924
stem: Paper 3 (History of Europe) essay practice. Plan for about 50 minutes.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Discuss the reasons why the Bolsheviks were able to remain in power between 1917 and 1924.
markscheme: Introduction with a clear argument ranking the main reasons
Popular early decrees: Decree on Peace and Decree on Land; Treaty of Brest-Litovsk (1918) ending the war at great cost
Repression: the Cheka, Red Terror, dissolution of the Constituent Assembly (January 1918)
Civil war victory: Trotsky's Red Army, conscription, use of former tsarist officers, control of the central heartland and railways
White weaknesses: divided leaders (Kolchak, Denikin, Yudenich), scattered geography, association with landlords and foreign intervention
War Communism securing resources for the army, despite its costs
Pragmatic flexibility: NEP (1921) after Kronstadt and peasant revolts; ban on factions
Lenin's leadership and party discipline; formation of the USSR (1922)
Historiography (e.g. Pipes on coercion versus social historians on popular support)
Conclusion weighing coercion against consent and flexibility
parts.notes: Real Paper 3 essays are marked out of 15 with markbands; this practice version uses a 10-point checklist. Expect more depth and precision than in Paper 2.
